note: Habitats a visitor can be briefed for. `id` matches game.js reef.biome (biomes advance in order; after the last, cycle). Add freely; the pipeline reads this, nothing is hardcoded. `pass_through`: scenery kinds creatures may swim/fly through in this biome (default none: everything registered is solid). Kinds: rock, coral, anemone, shrub, plus any new scenery's kind (a scenery prop's kind is its roster id). `scenery` (new biomes): [{id (roster model of kind scenery), count, spread cluster|scatter|edge|back, scale [min,max], phase 0-4 or phases [first,last] (copies spread across them), landmark (the last copy lands as its phase completes), pass_through}]. habitat.js places these props instead of the scene builder's own corals/tiers, keeping the phase progression: phase 0 = sparse ground cover, later phases bigger/rarer pieces. `frame`: {ground hex, water [shallow hex, deep hex], dens (fog multiplier), light (sun/caustics multiplier)} overrides the base frame. `scene`: base frame (ground, rocks, ground cover, light shafts, motes) and, for biomes without `scenery`, the scenery set habitat.js builds (reef, kelp, tidepool, mangrove, deep, meadow, canopy, jungle; default by medium). Optional when `scenery` + `frame` are given. `look`: the biome's identity (see `identity_rules`); briefs, habitat.js and the shelf diorama all read it. `neglect` (every biome with `scenery`): how this biome shows neglected tasks. {blight: roster id of kind scenery (the prop that spreads as tasks age; its own model, not one of the biome's `scenery` pieces), form (a word or two: overgrowth, mold, sand drift, ash fall, cobwebs, silt mat, rust, anything that fits the place), grows_on rocks|ground (where copies land: on the frame's rocks, or scattered over the ground), count 1-60 (copies at full blight, default 30), scale [min,max], murk (hex: what overdue tasks foul the water/air with), murk_name (a word for it: silt, dust haze, spore fog)}. habitat.js shows round(blight × count) copies, growing as blight rises, and tints toward `murk` as overdue tasks pile up.

identity_rules: Each biome owns one SHAPE LANGUAGE (e.g. branching, vertical ribbons, rounded clusters, arching roots, hanging, horizontal limbs). Its scenery and its creatures echo that shape; no other biome uses it as its main shape.
Each biome owns a HUE FAMILY (`look.palette`: sky/water, depth/horizon, ground, accent). Pick creature and plant colors from or next to it; avoid the main hues of the neighboring biomes.
`look.owns` lists motifs only this biome may use (scenery, creatures, plants). Never use a motif another biome owns.
Swap test: if this design would look at home in another biome with only a recolor, redesign it. Change at least two of: body plan, silhouette, pattern type, hue family, size class, motion.
Silhouette test: filled solid black at card size, the design should still say which biome it is from.
Motion signature (`look.motion`) sets the idle feel: match it (a deep creature drifts and pulses, a meadow one flits).
